messages.subject: change scales of size of points
parts:
Dear ggplot2 users,

Hi I want to change the default scales of size of points.
For example 

ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg)) + geom_point(aes(size = qsec))  

gives scales of size of points 15.5, 17.5, 20.5, 22.5.
However, I want to change the scales to 15.5,16.5,17.5, and equal or greater than 18.5.

Could you let me know how to do that?

I appreciate your kindness ahead :)

messages.author: d588a03e58ea7e7f
messages.subject: Re: change scales of size of points
parts:
On 9/19/2013 9:30 AM, Sophia wrote:
> Dear ggplot2 users,
>
> Hi I want to change the default scales of size of points.
> For example
>
> ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg)) + geom_point(aes(size = qsec))
>
> gives scales of size of points 15.5, 17.5, 20.5, 22.5.
> However, I want to change the scales to 15.5,16.5,17.5, and equal or
> greater than 18.5.
>
> Could you let me know how to do that?

ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg)) + geom_point(aes(size = qsec)) +
scale_size_continuous(breaks=c(15.5, 16.5, 17.5, 18.5))

Although something that you said makes me think that you don't
understand exactly what is happening here. This changes the values which
are displayed in the legend (guide); there is a continuous mapping
between the value of qsec and the size of the point. Only certain values
are shown in the legend because it is discrete (as a contrast, compare
the legend version of the guide for color to the colorbar version of the
guide for color). So the size of the dot shown for 18.5 is not the size
for 18.5 and greater; greater values have even larger sizes.

This is more apparent when you look at this plot, where I've replaced
one of the qsec with 30:

ggplot(transform(mtcars, qsec = c(30, qsec[-1])), aes(wt, mpg)) +
geom_point(aes(size = qsec)) +
scale_size_continuous(breaks=c(15.5, 16.5, 17.5, 18.5))

If you really want all values larger than some value to be the same,
either manually reset those values or cut the variable into categories
and use a discrete size scale.

--
Brian S. Diggs, PhD
Senior Research Associate, Department of Surgery
